layers.note: A tall herb of moist subalpine meadows and open subalpine forest; a root hemiparasite.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; often on cool slopes.

elevation_m.note: Montane to subalpine; about 1,000 m and up in Washington.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −20 to 1 °C; gone below −30 °C and above 5 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 7 to 18 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 21 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 700 to 3,200 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 400.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 1,700 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 80.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Bracted lousewort grows from British Columbia and Alberta to California and Colorado, in moist mountain meadows and woods (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
